prompt: If $\tan\theta = \frac{4}{3}$ and $\theta$ is in the first quadrant, find $\sec\theta$. Give a fraction or a decimal.

hints.text: $\sec\theta = \frac{5}{3}$, positive because $\theta$ is in quadrant I.

explanation: Taking the positive root (quadrant I makes everything positive) gives $\sec\theta = \frac{5}{3}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw the triangle
steps: $\tan\theta = \frac{4}{3}$ means opposite $4$, adjacent $3$, so the hypotenuse is $5$ — the $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle again.
